rationale: Collected every new/changed user-facing string on the branch (grep across the 51 changed non-test .go files' diff for fmt.Print*/fmt.Errorf/fmt.Fprint* and read each in context) and judged them as one set. The overwhelming majority is coherent: the 'note:' prefix used by the new IgnoredDirtNotice matches the two pre-existing 'note:' informational lines verbatim in form (lowercase, colon, no trailing punctuation on the label); the widespread pre-existing lowercase 'warning: <freetext>' convention (20+ sites) is extended by new code without deviation; every guard.NewFailure(msg, recovery) call this branch adds converges, by construction, on the spec-092-mandated machine-greppable 'recovery: <command>' trailing line, and the '<command>   (<parenthetical>)' three-space-before-paren shape is applied uniformly across every new recovery hint I found (repair.go, materialize.go, guard.go); the shared indeterminate-mode wording ('cannot determine mode: {reason}') is verbatim identical between internal/instruct/templates/indeterminate.md and internal/complete/complete.go's FormatResult tail leg, which is the one place the spec explicitly requires two arrival points to agree; and the new hook/dispatch.go indeterminate Block message correctly mirrors its nearest sibling (the pre-existing spec-093 implement-mode Block message's conditional-escape-hatch sub-pattern, 4-space indent, no 'Escape hatch:' label) rather than the unconditional protected-branch Block message's different sub-pattern, which is the right choice given both are spec/-branch-scoped conditional blocks. One genuine, isolated naming-convention break: internal/complete/materialize.go's two new residual-dirt warnings.

findings.title: New WARN line invents a dotted-namespace name found nowhere else in the codebase, breaking the kebab-case convention every sibling WARN line (including one in the same file's own command) follows
findings.detail: internal/complete/materialize.go lines 431 and 433 (new in this branch) print: `fmt.Fprintf(in.warnWriter, "WARN complete.residual_artifact_dirt: %v (survived materialization; non-blocking per ADR-0025)\n", ...)`. Every other WARN-prefixed line in the entire codebase names its subject in plain kebab-case with no namespace prefix: internal/complete/complete.go:1601's printResultWarnings renders `WARN %s: %s` from validate.Issue.Name, and its own doc comment lists the real examples it prints — `cmd-docs`, `missing-source-globs`, `adr-divergence-proposed` (all validate.AddWarning call sites across internal/validate/*.go use the same kebab-case scheme: `unclaimed-source`, `adr-divergence-attribute`, etc., never a dot). internal/approve/impl.go:1169 uses the identical `WARN %s: %s` renderer. Most tellingly, internal/complete/bead_scope.go:121 — a sibling in the SAME package as the new lines — prints `WARN bead-scope: %s is owned by domain %s...`, i.e. kebab-case, no dot, immediately adjacent in spirit to the new code. `complete.residual_artifact_dirt` is the only WARN name anywhere that combines a dotted namespace prefix with snake_case, and a real `mindspec complete <bead>` invocation can print it on the same warnWriter stream as the printResultWarnings-rendered kebab-case lines (both are reachable from internal/complete's materialization path), so a user sees two visually similar 'WARN <name>: <message>' lines using two incompatible naming schemes side by side in one command's output. This is a per-bead-panel blind spot exactly of the kind the final review exists to catch: bead 6/8's own panels would have seen this string in isolation and had no sibling WARN line in view to compare it against.
findings.evidence: internal/complete/materialize.go:431,433; internal/complete/complete.go:1588-1601 (printResultWarnings + doc comment naming cmd-docs/missing-source-globs/adr-divergence-proposed as its examples); internal/complete/bead_scope.go:121 (`WARN bead-scope: ...`); internal/approve/impl.go:1169; internal/validate/docsync.go:124,142,658 and internal/validate/divergence.go (every AddWarning/AddError name is kebab-case, zero dotted names in the codebase). Pinned by internal/complete/complete_test.go:2850 (`strings.Contains(captured.String(), "WARN complete.residual_artifact_dirt")`), confirming the string is deliberate and test-locked, not a typo that slipped through untested.
findings.recommendation: Rename to the codebase's established kebab-case, unprefixed scheme (e.g. `WARN residual-artifact-dirt: ...`), consistent with `bead-scope` in the same file's own package and with every validate.Issue.Name in the repo. Update the pinned assertion in internal/complete/complete_test.go:2850 to match. If the intent was specifically to disambiguate which command emitted the warning (unlike bead-scope's warnings, which only ever fire from `mindspec complete`), that's already true of every other WARN line here too (they all only fire from `mindspec complete`), so no site needs a namespace prefix to stay unambiguous to the reader.

concrete_changes_required: internal/complete/materialize.go lines 431 and 433: rename the warning name from `complete.residual_artifact_dirt` to a kebab-case name with no dotted namespace (e.g. `residual-artifact-dirt`), matching every other WARN-line name in the codebase (`bead-scope`, `cmd-docs`, `missing-source-globs`, `adr-divergence-proposed`, etc.) — this is the only dotted+snake_case WARN name anywhere in the tree and it prints on the same stream, in the same command, as the kebab-case ones.
internal/complete/complete_test.go:2850: update the pinned string assertion from `WARN complete.residual_artifact_dirt` to match the renamed warning.
